title: Assessing Covariate-Informed Grid Load Forecasting with a Time-Series Foundation Model
note: arXiv record, v1 only (2026-09-06), authors Pendyala, Fu, Yan, Virani; presented at IJCNN 2026. Chronos-2 on ISO New England and ENTSO-E load against task-specific deep models: fine-tuning helps a lot and it is good at short horizons; zero-shot trails the task-specific models and its error grows faster with horizon. No code or data link on the page.

title: Assessing Covariate-Informed Grid Load Forecasting with a Time-Series Foundation Model (full text, setup)
note: Setup. Daily data, not hourly: ISO-NE 8 zones, train 2011-2020, test 2021 (365 days), aggregation to daily not stated; ENTSO-E 6 countries, daily peak from hourly, train 2015-2018, test 2019 (365 days). Horizons 30, 60, 90 days, error averaged over day 1..H; 30-day history for every model. Metric MAPE (Chronos-2 median). Authors are at GE Vernova research.

title: Assessing Covariate-Informed Grid Load Forecasting with a Time-Series Foundation Model (full text, covariates and baselines)
note: Covariates: calendar plus dew point and dry-bulb temperature (ISO-NE); calendar plus temperature and two radiation series (ENTSO-E), supplied over history and horizon. Whether future weather is observed or forecast is not stated. Baselines TCN, LSTM, Transformer trained per dataset with target and covariates and the same 30-day history; an identical covariate set is not explicitly confirmed.
